about_drives_p1: Most of my best work started as a bug. Footsteps playing the wrong surface, a SoundBank eating twice its budget. On *Not Today Darling*, four players shared one screen and one audio budget — every sound had to earn its place.
about_drives_p2: I build tools when something wastes my time twice. Wwise kept breaking after Perforce pulls on *Shadow Frames*, so I wrote a script to fix it. Now the whole team uses it.
about_journey_p1: Started with classical piano, then switched to physics and math — I wanted to know why sound works, not just how to play it. That eventually led to programming audio systems in C++ and Python.
about_journey_p2: Third year at DAE in Belgium now. Built a real-time beatbox classifier when off-the-shelf ML tools couldn't keep up. Wrote Wwise repair scripts because fixing broken references by hand after every merge got old fast.
about_page_description: Game audio designer and developer studying at DAE Belgium.
achievement_games_desc: Led audio implementation on 4 games at DAE (Wwise, MetaSounds, FMOD). Sound design contributions to 8+ additional projects.
achievement_thesis_desc: Unity + ElevenLabs API prototype for real-time AI audio generation. Built predictive buffering to mask latency. Tested limits of generative audio in games.
achievement_tools_desc: Built 2 pipeline tools: Wwise Unreal Fixer and Unreal Engine Rebuilder
cta_desc: Looking for 2026 internship in game audio. 3-6 months, EU passport, relocation-ready.
philosophy_quote: If players can't hear the enemy approaching because the ambient is too loud, that's not an artistic choice - it's a bug.
